issue_context.title: `UnsafeAccessor` works on non-static methods
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-runtime-compilerservices See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
```C# class InstanceAccessors { public InstanceAccessors() { } [UnsafeAccessor(UnsafeAccessorKind.Constructor)] public extern InstanceAccessors UnsafeNonStaticAccessorForConstructor(); } void Test() { (new InstanceAccessors()).InstanceAccessors(); // Works } ``` Per the proposal https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/81741, the attribute should only be effective on static methods. It's also not clear what it means on instance methods. @AaronRobinsonMSFT
Author: vitek-karas
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Runtime.CompilerServices`
Milestone: -

> the attribute should only be effective on static methods

Yep. I will add a run-time check for CoreCLR and a compile time check in NativeAOT.

/cc @fanyang-mono @jkotas

review_comments: Do we also throw for generic `UnsafeAccessor` methods, and `UnsafeAccessor` methods in generic types? I do not see the test for it.
No, we do not. I just verified the lookup fails. I will add tests.
